key_insight: Sb doping creates bright, delocalized excitons in Cs2BInCl6, while Na-to-K alloying mainly reshapes self-trapped exciton distortions and tunes photoluminescence without strongly affecting absorption.
engineering_relevance: This gives a composition handle for engineering lead-free double perovskite emitters with tunable color and polarization fingerprints for optoelectronic design.
method: Optical spectroscopy on Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals with B-site alloying from Na to K.
Ab initio calculations of excitonic states, lattice distortion, and self-trapped excitons.
Time-resolved polarization anisotropy measurements to test wavefunction-dependent emission predictions.
evidence_signal: PL shifts from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV while absorption near 3.8 eV stays nearly unchanged, and measured anisotropy matches theory.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on nanoscale composition control and careful spectroscopy, so disorder or synthesis variability could blur the predicted anisotropy and PL trends.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
